primitives.note: Rupture (delayed AoE), Feral Scream (cone), Feast (single-target) each deal damage on cast/short delay, on cooldown, for mana
mana costs (50/70-90/30/100) against Cho'Gath's mana pool can gate how many casts fit into the 15s window, especially W's rank-scaling cost and R's flat 100
Vorpal Spikes arms the next 3 basic attacks (within 6s) to fire an on-attack magic damage blast; E itself has no cast time and deals no direct damage
Vorpal Spikes resets Cho'Gath's basic attack timer when cast, letting an immediate empowered auto follow
each empowered attack deals bonus magic damage equal to a % of the target's maximum health (a champion-dummy target uses the champion formula, not the capped monster formula)

permanent Feast stacks (gained only on a Feast kill) grant Cho'Gath bonus health that feeds R's own damage (10% bonus health) and add +0.5%/stack to E's max-health-% damage term; needs an assumed stack count for the fight

needsBespoke.why: Rupture/Feral Scream/Feast are plain-cast nukes, Vorpal Spikes is a standard empowered-attack+attack-reset onhit rider with a target-max-health-% conditional term, and the Feast-stack interplay (bonus health -> R and E damage) is exactly what the infinite-scaling primitive covers once a stack count is assumed. No mechanic here (recasts, channels, forms, stance changes, ammo systems) falls outside the listed primitives.

unsettled.question: Is Feast's noted +8/+12/+16 (per rank) damage increase per Feast stack an additional additive term on top of Feast#RDamage/RMonsterDamage (base + 50% AP + 10% bonus health), or is it fully explained by the 10% bonus-health ratio already applied to the bonus health each stack grants?
options: It is a separate flat additive term per stack not present in the sheet's RDamage/RMonsterDamage calculations
It is not a separate term; it is the wiki's shorthand for the 10% bonus-health ratio acting on the RHealthPerStack bonus health from each stack
Moot in the dummy fight because the simulator assumes 0 Feast stacks throughout
quotes: Each stack of ''Feast'' increases the damage by {{ap|8|12|16}}.

unsettled.question: What Feast stack count (and thus bonus health) should be assumed for the 15s single-target-dummy damage fight, given the dummy 'never fights back' and has substantial health so a Feast kill is unlikely?
options: 0 stacks: no pre-fight stacks assumed and none gained mid-fight since the dummy never dies
A nonzero pre-fight stack count representing a mid/late-game Cho'Gath who has picked up stacks before the encounter
1+ stacks if the dummy's health/resists are set low enough that Feast's true damage executes it, granting a stack mid-fight
quotes: If this attack kills the target, '''Cho'Gath''' gains a permanent ''Feast'' {{tip|stack}} that infinitely stacks.

Each stack of ''Feast'' increases the cast range of the ability by {{fd|2.5}}, for a maximum increase of 25 at 10 stacks, and grants '''Cho'Gath''' {{as|{{sti|health|'''bonus''' health}}}} as well as {{sti|range|'''bonus''' attack range}} and increased {{tip|size}}, capping at {{sti|range|75 '''bonus''' attack range}} and 100% increased size.

unsettled.question: Within Vorpal Spikes' 6s empowerment window, is the target-max-health-% damage term (and its per-stack buzzword bonus) evaluated using the Feast stack count at the moment each of the 3 empowered attacks lands, or fixed at the moment E is cast?
options: Recomputed per landed attack using the current stack count at that instant
Fixed for all 3 attacks based on the stack count when E was cast

proposal: Open with Rupture (Q) on the dummy; it deals magic damage after its cast time plus a short delay.
Follow with Feral Scream (W) for its cone magic damage.
Cast Vorpal Spikes (E) to arm the next 3 basic attacks and get the free attack-timer reset, then auto-attack immediately to start consuming the empowered attacks.
Cast Feast (R) as soon as it is in range and off cooldown for a burst of true damage scaled off Cho'Gath's bonus health; recast it every time its long cooldown (60-80s) comes back up.

Between ability casts, keep auto-attacking so all 3 Vorpal Spikes charges land inside the 6s window before it expires, and recast E again as soon as its cooldown (which starts only after the charges are used) is available.
Recast Rupture and Feral Scream on cooldown for the remainder of the 15s, weaving auto attacks (empowered when available) in the gaps.
Track mana spend across Q/W/E/R casts; if mana runs low, prioritize E (cheapest, enables onhit damage) and R (highest single hit) over repeated W casts.
questions: At what level and with what item build does the simulator run this fight, and is mana actually a binding constraint at that build (affecting whether all four abilities can be cast repeatedly for 15s)?
Should Feast (R) be assumed pre-charged/off cooldown at the start of the fight, or does its 60-80s cooldown mean it is realistically cast at most once or twice within 15s?

What Feast-stack count (see unsettled question above) should the rotation assume Cho'Gath enters the fight with, since it changes both R's own damage and E's per-hit scaling, and thus whether R or auto-attack-heavy E play is prioritized?

Is Vorpal Spikes best recast immediately every time it's available (maximizing onhit uptime) even if it interrupts otherwise-queued Q/W casts, or should Q/W be prioritized first each time they're off cooldown?
